title: Primary and secondary data in psychology
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:36Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank card defines primary and secondary research clearly, but it never says secondary data must be judged for quality, which is a core part of this brief, so a match would teach an incomplete idea.

draft.title: Primary and secondary data
card: Data the researcher collects first-hand for their own study, such as by running an experiment, a survey or an observation.
Data that was collected by other people and is reused. It can come from journal articles, books, government reports or online sources.
Secondary data can be quicker and cheaper to find. But the researcher did not control how it was collected, so they cannot be sure it is good.
Secondary data must be judged for quality before it is used. Check who collected it, how they collected it and whether the source can be trusted.
draft.remember: Primary data is gathered by you. Secondary data is gathered by others, so check its quality.

opts: A student reads a published study on sleep and memory
A student times how long peers take to finish a puzzle
A student surveys her class about their daily screen use
A student watches children play and records what happens
a.why: The student reads results that other researchers collected, so the data is secondary. The other three options each involve the student collecting the data first-hand, which makes it primary.

b.q: Priya wants to compare teenage sleep in Victoria. She uses a government report on sleep that she did not collect herself. What should she do before relying on it?
opts: Check how the data was collected and by whom
Treat it as reliable because it is from a government
Call it primary data because she chose to use it
Use it without checking, as it saves her time
b.why: The report is secondary data, so Priya did not control how it was gathered. She needs to judge its quality first. A trusted source can still have flaws, and choosing data does not make it primary.
b.clue: She did not collect it, so she cannot know how good it is yet.

a.best: A student reads a published study on sleep and memory

b.best: Check how the data was collected and by whom
